headline: Westpac's APRA Level 2 (Group) CET1 capital ratio rose 4 basis points in FY25, from 12.49% at 30 September 2024 to 12.53% at 30 September 2025 (results announcement capital table). The results announcement states the increase came from net profit less the payment of the 2024 final and 2025 interim ordinary dividends, other reserve movements and lower capitalised software balances, offset by higher Total RWA and on-market share buybacks; Total RWA increased $12.6 billion. The investor discussion pack's key capital ratios table confirms the same levels (12.5% Sep-24, 12.5% Sep-25). The bank publishes only a half-on-half (Mar-25 to Sep-25) CET1 capital walk, not a full-year walk, so the full-year drivers are quantified only qualitatively.

disagreements.topic: Main driver of the $12.6bn Total RWA increase
values: Results announcement narrative: 'Total RWA increased by $12.6 billion mainly from higher Interest Rate Risk in the banking book (IRRBB) RWA.'
Investor discussion pack full-year RWA walk: Lending +$12.6bn, IRRBB -$2.0bn
disagreements.preferred: Investor discussion pack RWA walk (Lending +$12.6bn as main driver)
disagreements.explanation: The results announcement narrative attributes the $12.6bn RWA increase mainly to IRRBB, but the investor pack's full-year RWA walk (the primary decomposition of the same comparison) shows Lending +$12.6bn as the main driver and IRRBB -$2.0bn. The two documents disagree on which component drove the RWA increase.

limitations: The bank does not publish a full-year (Sep-24 to Sep-25) Level 2 CET1 capital walk; the only published walk is half-on-half (Mar-25 to Sep-25), which is a different comparison. Per the method, its bars are not used as this comparison's contributions; they are described in the narratives only.

The full-year drivers (net profit, dividends, RWA, capital deductions, buybacks) are quantified only qualitatively from the results announcement narrative; no full-year bps figures are published for them.
The results announcement narrative and the investor pack RWA walk disagree on the main driver of the $12.6bn RWA increase (IRRBB vs Lending); this is reported as a disagreement.

The residual of +4 bps equals the total movement; because the individual drivers are not quantified in bps for the full-year comparison, the residual is the full movement rather than an unexplained remainder.
Basis normalised from 'cash' to 'ex_notables': no page in evidence prints 'cash' beside the movement, and the registry names ex_notables as the bank's headline basis.

evidence_records.quote: The Level 2 CET1 capital ratio was 12.53% at 30 September 2025, 4 basis points higher than 30 September 2024. The increase from net profit less the payment of 2024 final ordinary dividend and 2025 interim ordinary dividend, other reserve movements and lower capitalised software balances was offset by higher Total RWA and on market share buybacks. Total RWA increased by $12.6 billion mainly from higher Interest Rate Risk in the banking book (IRRBB) RWA.
The CET1 capital ratio increased 4 basis points as net profit was largely offset by the payment of dividends and increases in Risk Weighted Assets (RWA).
The Level 2 CET1 capital ratio at 30 September 2025 was 12.53%, 29 basis points higher than 31 March 2025.
Second Half 2025 net profit: 80 basis points increase;
Payment of the 2025 interim ordinary dividend: 58 basis points reduction;
RWA movement: 7 basis points decrease mainly from higher credit RWA partly offset by lower non-credit RWA;
Capital deductions and other items: 16 basis points increase mainly from other reserve movements and lower capitalised software balances; and
Capital return: 2 basis points reduction due to the on market share buyback.
